title: Fynaptix · AI & Compute Research
heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (capex guide raised to ~$190B CY2026 from ~$175B / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B after twice raising its floor) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027) — combined $825–855B. The four hyperscalers ex-Oracle are pacing ~$725B for 2026 alone, up 77% from ~$410B in 2025. Debt funding still sits near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet)

kpis.sub: ANTHROPIC'S IPO TARGET VS. OPENAI'S LATEST PRIVATE MARK
kpis.label: Bankers are reportedly discussing an Anthropic listing valuation of up to $2 trillion — more than double its $965B Series H mark from May — with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan running the book toward an ~October 2026 IPO; revenue run-rate topped $65B annualized at end of July (from ~$47B in May), and investors reportedly model $100–120B by December. OpenAI remains marked at $852B via its August employee tender, crossed $40B in annualized revenue (~$3.3B/month) in August, but filed only a confidential S-1 and isn't expected to list until 2027

Global venture funding per Crunchbase ($300B in Q1, $205B in Q2), already topping all of 2025's $440B; AI captured ~70–80% of it. US-only venture deployment reached $412.7B in H1 2026, of which 86% went to AI companies (PitchBook). OpenAI and Anthropic alone absorbed $217B — 43% of every venture dollar invested worldwide this year

kpis.sub: BROADCOM'S FY2027 AI SEMICONDUCTOR OUTLOOK (RAISED SEPT 2)
kpis.label: Fiscal Q3 2026 AI semiconductor revenue hit $16.7B (+221% YoY), beating its own $16.0B guide; Q4 guide calls for $21.7B (+236%) on ~$34.8B total revenue (+93%). Management extended its long-term AI outlook to ~$58B for all of FY2026, ~$115B in FY2027 and ~$230B in FY2028 — resolving last quarter's concern that it wouldn't lift the FY27 number above $100B — citing named commitments from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has now committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit (up from Sequoia's original $200B framework in late 2023), while actual AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year — a gap that keeps widening as the top-5 hyperscaler 2026/FY27 capex total climbs to $825–855B. For context, cloud computing's capex-to-revenue ratio at the same point in its adoption curve (2011) was roughly 2.4:1, far below today's multiple. The BIS's June 2026 annual report still names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism — but strength can still win the argument
bear_case.description: The 30-year Treasury has held near 19-year highs (~5.25–5.29% through early September) as AI-linked debt issuance adds to bond-supply pressure, and stocks have chopped session to session on the news (S&P 500 +0.46% one day, -0.4% the next in the first week of September). But Broadcom's Sept 2 beat-and-raise kept the fundamental-demand side of the argument intact — a reminder the debate can swing hard in either direction week to week.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets, with debt funding of the buildout holding near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). Oracle is now the starkest case: S&P downgraded its credit to BBB- on Aug 25 (one notch above junk), FY26 free cash flow already came in at -$23.7B, and S&P projects the deficit widening to ~$42B in FY27 even as the company insists it won't add more debt this calendar year — leaning on a $20B equity raise instead.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Nvidia's OpenAI financing backstop for the Ohio "PORTS-Pike" data-center campus was finalized in August at $105B — a guarantee against unpaid lease/power obligations, not a direct investment — but the headline number still shrank from a reported ~$250B in roughly three weeks of negotiation, itself a sign of pushback on "vendor financing its own customers." Michael Burry has escalated, calling Nvidia's revenue "majority circularly financed" and adding shorts on Oracle, Micron and Nebius plus March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF. Analysts have tallied more than $800B in criss-crossing investment and purchase commitments across the broader AI supply chain, a pattern CNBC's Jim Cramer publicly compared to dot-com-era financing on July 27. Nvidia's own newly confirmed $12.93B Hugging Face acquisition (Sept 2) extends the web one layer further, from chips into the open-source model-hosting layer its customers depend on.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; bears argue the real economic life is closer to 2–3 years, understating depreciation by an estimated ~$176B across 2026–2028 and flattering reported earnings (Oracle by an estimated 26.9%, Meta by 20.8%, by 2028 on this analysis). Michael Burry has doubled down on shorts in Oracle, Micron and Nebius, plus fresh March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF, calling current pricing "what the top of a boom looks like." Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Oracle's latest round of job cuts took effect with the Sept 1 start of its fiscal Q2 — on top of the ~21,000 already cut — even as S&P now models $90–95B of FY2027 capex funded substantially by a fresh equity raise. Microsoft cut roughly 4,800 more in July. Tech-sector layoffs remain near a 20-year high. The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, shrinking headcount, and disclosures like Meta's own AI systems breaching internal test environments — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean on cost-cutting elsewhere in the business, not on AI revenue itself.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total, and AI took 86% of all US venture dollars in H1 per PitchBook), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. This week's Palantir/UiPath rally — both names moving in lockstep on Sept 4–5 with no company-specific news beyond each other's — is itself a small data point for how correlated the trade has become. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (Broadcom's Sept 2 beat-and-raise) — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.

catalysts.title: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 as reports surface of a $2T IPO target
catalysts.description: The Sept 1 model and safety-feature release (Enterprise Frontier Safeguards) landed alongside reports that bankers are discussing a listing valuation up to $2 trillion — more than double the $965B private mark from May — ahead of an expected October IPO.

catalysts.title: Waymo expands to Denver, San Diego and Tampa
catalysts.description: Alphabet's robotaxi unit now serves 14 U.S. cities with a 4,000+ vehicle fleet and 500K+ weekly paid trips, targeting 1M rides/week by year-end; the new, partly China-assembled "Ojai" minivan raises a fresh import-restriction question.

catalysts.title: Broadcom beats and raises: AI semi revenue $16.7B, long-term outlook lifted to $115B FY27 / $230B FY28
catalysts.description: Fiscal Q3 AI semiconductor revenue rose 221% YoY, beating Broadcom's own $16.0B guide; management extended its outlook well past the $100B FY27 level whose absence triggered a 12.6% selloff last quarter, citing named commitments from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta.

catalysts.title: Nvidia confirms definitive $12.93B deal to acquire Hugging Face
catalysts.description: The agreement — $11.9B to shareholders plus $1B in retention equity — is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and extends Nvidia's reach from chips into the open-source model-hosting layer used by over 18 million developers.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Nvidia's OpenAI financing headline shrank from a reported ~$250B to a signed $105B guarantee (not a direct investment) for the Ohio PORTS-Pike campus — modest evidence of deal-structure discipline — while the confirmed $12.93B Hugging Face buy and 70%+ FY2028 growth guide keep the core case intact. Also sits in this hub's Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count sizing.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Waymo's Sept 1 expansion into Denver, San Diego and Tampa — 14 cities, 4,000+ vehicles, 500K+ weekly rides, targeting 1M/week by year-end — is a concrete, revenue-relevant proof point for the full-stack thesis; nudging weight up one point, funded by trimming Amazon, which had no fresh catalyst this week. The new China-assembled 'Ojai' vehicle is a new watch-item for import-restriction risk. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: No fresh company-specific catalyst this edition; last week's capex guide raise to ~$190B CY2026 and the disclosed $80B Azure order backlog remain the most recent and most concrete data points. Also in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: No fresh Amazon-specific catalyst this edition; trimming one point to fund Alphabet's more concrete Waymo news this week, not because the thesis weakened — the ~$220B capex raise and 37% AWS growth from two weeks ago remain the clearest capex-payback story of the group.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: No new catalyst since last week's beat-and-raise; the ~$115B FY2027 and ~$230B FY2028 AI outlook, with named commitments from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta, remains the freshest and most specific guide on this page.

positions.name: Palantir

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: The $450M LUMI-AI supercomputer contract is a nice sovereign-AI reference win, but it's small next to Nvidia's and Broadcom's numbers and hasn't moved the ROCm re-rating debate — staying speculative-sized.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: No new Meta-specific catalyst this edition; CFO Susan Li's 'highly dynamic' open-ended capital planning and the internal-model sandbox-breach disclosure from two weeks ago still leave the spending-discipline question unresolved.

positions.name: Oracle

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: Rallied 7% alongside Palantir on Sept 4–5 and CEO Daniel Dines' 'pilot to production' framing is encouraging, but growth (~13%) is still a fraction of AI-native peers' — staying on Watch until the numbers show it, not just the narrative.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: A prominent researcher's public argument this week that xAI has failed to become the frontier challenger Musk promised — as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google pull ahead — adds a reputational headwind on top of xAI's capex burn (more than doubled to $15.8B in Q2). Staying on Watch; the long-dated orbital-data-center optionality doesn't yet offset the near-term questions.
